title: POC retention matrix and redaction playbook
body:
Purpose
-----
This doc is a working playbook for customer POCs that need: clear retention rules, pragmatic redaction strategies, and candidate DPA addenda language we can iterate with Legal and the customer. Focus is on minimal friction for Solutions Engineering during short-term POCs while preserving a path to hardened contract terms for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Audience: SEs, Eng architects, Legal review, Customer security/infosec reviewers.
- Scope: short-term POCs (1–12 weeks) and pre-production pilots. Not the final production DPA, but includes candidate addenda clauses.

Quick summary upfront (TL;DR)
----------------------------
- Default retention for transcript/interaction data during a POC: 30 days, auto-delete unless customer requests extension.
- Short-lived debugging artifacts (logs, traces): 7 days by default; can be extended to 30d on request and contract.
- Hand-curated eval datasets and prompts: owner-controlled; by default not stored in customer-shared inference logs.
- Redaction first: implement automated PII detection + deterministic redaction pipeline before storing any user content when customer asks.
- Offer two addenda templates: "POC temporary retention" (fast) and "Pilot-to-Prod transition" (longer-term).

Retention matrix (practical mapping for SEs)
-------------------------------------------
Column headers: Data class | Typical content examples | Default POC retention | Storage location | Redaction required? | Notes
1) Interaction transcripts | chat messages, prompts, responses | 30 days | Redwood-hosted ephemeral bucket (tagged poc/<customer>) | optional (see customer preference) | default for most POCs; if PHI/PII suspected, reduce to 7 days and enable redaction
2) Model input artifacts | full prompts, attachments | 30 days | same as transcripts (separate prefix) | recommended | discourage attaching raw files; prefer sanitized snippets
3) Debug logs & traces | stack traces, GPU dumps, request headers | 7 days | logging pipeline (retention policy tag = poc-logs) | always strip auth tokens | include sample scrubbers in engineer checklist
4) KV cache / prefix cache snapshots | cached token material for latency tests | 0 days (ephemeral in-memory) | never persist to object store for POC | not applicable | use in-memory only; persist only for reproducibility by explicit customer consent
5) Aggregated metrics | latency, token counts, error rates | 365 days (aggregated) | metrics DB with customer-id tag | no | used for capacity planning & billing; never link to raw user text in analytics views
6) Hand-curated evals | labeled prompt -> expected output | customer owned | per customer agreement | depends on dataset | treat as customer intellectual property; do not include in generic training pools

Redaction playbook (engineering steps)
-------------------------------------
Goal: remove or mask high-risk entities before storing. Prioritize automation, but allow human review only when customer explicitly allows.
Steps: 
1) Pre-ingest rules: block known-sensitive attachments (e.g., files > 10MB, binaries). Return a 400 with guidance to upload to secure sftp if needed.
2) Entity detection: run PII/PHI detector (off-the-shelf model + customer custom regex list). Tag entities into classes: NAME, EMAIL, SSN, CREDIT_CARD, MEDICAL_RECORD, IP, ADDRESS, PHONE.
3) Redaction strategy: default = token replacement using deterministic placeholders (e.g., [REDACTED_EMAIL:hash]). For legal review we can provide reversible pseudonymization with HMAC-based salt under custody rules.
4) Hashing for safe analysis: if customer wants counts, store hashed tokens (sha256 with per-customer salt stored in KMS) rather than plaintext.
5) Human review: only allowed if customer checked opt-in in the POC intake form; require audit logging and explicit legal sign-off.
6) Validation: automated QA to re-run detector on redacted text and assert no remaining high-risk patterns.

Sample redaction policy snippets (for quick copy/paste)
----------------------------------------------------
- "Redaction ON: All user-supplied free-text is scanned for sensitive entities. Matched entities will be replaced with deterministic placeholders prior to being written to persistent storage. Reversible pseudonymization is available with explicit written consent."
- "Debug logs: stack traces are scrubbed for tokens and IPs. Any logged user content must be redacted as above; if un-redacted content is required for troubleshooting, it will be delivered via secure transfer and not stored in Redwood buckets more than 72 hours."

Candidate DPA addendum language (POC-focused)
---------------------------------------------
- Clause A (Retention cap): "For the duration of the POC, Provider will retain Customer Interaction Data for a maximum of thirty (30) days after collection, unless Customer elects in writing to extend retention for documented debugging or evaluation purposes."
- Clause B (Redaction & Pseudonymization): "Provider will apply automated redaction/pseudonymization to detect and mask sensitive identifiers prior to persistent storage. Re-identification/material reversal requires Customer written authorization."
- Clause C (Debug escrow): "If debug artifacts are required beyond default retention windows, Provider will provision a time-limited secure escrow and will delete remaining copies upon completion of debugging; Customer will receive a copy by secure transfer on request."

Risk, assumptions and operational caveats
----------------------------------------
- Assumption: PII/PHI detection models are not 100% recall; customers with high regulatory requirements should use Private deployment and on-prem data handling.
- Risk: Deterministic redaction can leak via surrounding context in corner cases; recommend pseudonymization + context-stripping for regulated customers.
- Operational caveat: Automated redaction introduces latency; measure and warn customers if latency SLOs matter (e.g., <200ms).

Engineer checklist for POC onboarding
----------------------------------
- [ ] POC intake form completed (data classes, examples, required retention window)
- [ ] Security questionnaire received and initial risk tier assigned (low/medium/high)
- [ ] Redaction level selected (none / redaction / pseudonymization)
- [ ] Logging retention tags configured: poc-logs, poc-transcripts, poc-metrics
- [ ] KMS key created for pseudonymization salts if requested
- [ ] Legal provided DPA addendum template version for customer sign-off
- [ ] Monitoring alert for any unredacted sensitive content matches (auto-block + SE slack alert)

Operational patterns and recommended POC templates
------------------------------------------------
- Fast POC template (non-regulated): default 30d transcript retention, 7d logs, redaction optional. Use hosted API with customer tokenization and limited attachments allowed.
- Sensitive POC template: 7d transcript retention, redaction enforced, debug escrow only with signed exception, use Dedicated or Private if scale/SLAs required.
- Transition plan: before moving to Dedicated/Private, run a 2-week compliance audit: export all retained artifacts, validate redaction efficacy, and produce a short report for Legal and customer security.

Open questions for Legal and Security
------------------------------------
- Do we need a formal standard for the maximum allowable re-identification risk metric for POCs? (e.g., target false negative < 0.5% for named entities)
- When reversible pseudonymization is enabled, what is the standard retention for the salt/key material? Can customer hold the key exclusively?
- Approval workflow: what minimum evidentiary artifacts does Legal need before approving human-in-the-loop reviews?

Next steps (short-term)
----------------------
1) Run this playbook with 2 active POCs this quarter (SE owners: Ari Kaplan and Samir Patel).
2) Collect performance metrics on redaction latency impact and false positives/negatives.
3) Iterate candidate addendum language with Legal (owner: Maya Gupta).
4) Publish a short SE one-pager + intake form template and link in Confluence.

Notes to self / scratches
-------------------------
- Need quick scripts to scrub stack traces: see github/retention-scripts sample.
- Customer A asked for 90d retention for audit. Default will be 30d; prepare justification and exception process.
- Remember to tag all S3 objects with poc=<customer> and sensitivity=<low|med|high>.

Revision history
----------------
- 2024-11-20: initial draft (Maya)
- 2024-12-09: added redaction playbook and sample DPA clauses (Ari)
- 2025-02-09: minor edits to retention matrix and checklist (Samir)

End of doc
